extracted.intended_audience: English citizens and policymakers (late 18th-century readers interested in fiscal and social reform)
extracted.subtask_description: A programmatic plan for reducing national taxation and current expenses, abolishing the old poor-law system, and reallocating surplus revenue to direct relief (child allowances, pensions, education, employment asylums, and other targeted supports). Includes concrete budget lines and administrative proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit public salaries to service value
rubrics_metrics.description: No public servant should be paid beyond the value of the services they perform; 'it is impossible that any service he can perform, can merit from a nation more than ten thousand pounds a year; and as no man should be paid beyond his services...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public money 'ought to be touched with the most scrupulous consciousness of honour.' Salary caps and scrupulous justification of pay are recommended to curb extravagant offices and expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce national peace establishment to L1,500,000
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed peace establishment of L1,500,000 annually divided as: Navy L500,000; Army L500,000; Expenses of Government L500,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as a reasonable benchmark (still six times greater than American expenses) and as an achievable target given abolition of foreign intrigues and alliance with France; used as basis for calculating available surplus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three hundred representatives are sufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Three hundred representatives, fairly elected, are sufficient for legislative purposes and preferable to a larger number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowance proposed at 500 pounds per annum per representative (accounting for non-attendance) yielding L75,000 if all attend for six months; representation viewed as honourable and allowance only to defray expenses, not as an office of profit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured official department salary schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: A recommended configuration of official offices and salaries totaling L497,500 (e.g., three offices at L10,000; ten at L5,000; twenty at L2,000; forty at L1,000; etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list is illustrative, 'not an exact detail of offices, but to show the number of rate of salaries which five hundred thousand pounds will support.' Suggests administrative economies and the option to deduct 4% from offices to create a L20,000 slot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abolish poor-rates and remit equivalent taxes to the poor
rubrics_metrics.description: First step of relief: abolish the poor-rates entirely and, in place of them, remit taxes to the poor of double the amount of the present poor-rates (total proposed remission: four millions annually).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This remission is framed as direct, visible relief (unlike some excise reductions) and is estimated to benefit both the poor and house-keepers by two millions each; presented as superior to the existing poor-law machinery and litigation costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child allowance for poor families: L4 per child under 14
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay, as a remission of taxes to every poor family, four pounds a year for every child under fourteen years of age (targeting 630,000 children; cost L2,520,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim is to relieve parents' poverty and promote education; this measure replaces poor-rates and is expected to reduce future poverty by removing the expense of raising children as a cause of destitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education requirement tied to child allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Parents receiving the child allowance are enjoined to send children to school to learn reading, writing, and common arithmetic; ministers of every parish to certify jointly to an office that this duty is performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linking financial relief to schooling both improves future prospects and reduces ignorance; ministers' joint certification provides administrative oversight and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pension scheme for aged persons: L6 (50–60) and L10 (60+)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide each person aged 50–60 L6 per annum, and each person aged 60+ L10 per annum, for a proposed cohort of 140,000 claimants (70,000 in each age band) costing L1,120,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The support is cast as a right (not charity), justified by lifetime contribution in taxes; calculation given comparing taxes paid over life and the sum received in old age; intended to render aged persons 'comfortable.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Target number of aged claimants and eligibility assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate that one-third of all persons aged 50+ (assumed 140,000 of 420,000) may at some time require support; of these 70,000 are 50–60 and 70,000 are 60+.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This eligibility estimate is used to budget the pension scheme; accepts margin for accidents and economic dislocation across classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education grants for families slightly above poverty
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide ten shillings a year for six years (six months' schooling each year) and a half-crown for paper and spelling books to each of an estimated 400,000 children; annual cost L250,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This targets children not counted among the poorest but who would otherwise lack schooling; reasoned as investment to reduce future poverty and inequality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Birth and marriage donations of twenty shillings
rubrics_metrics.description: Give twenty shillings on the birth of a child to every woman who claims it (estimated one-fourth of 200,000 births → L50,000) and twenty shillings to newly-married couples who claim (estimated L20,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small, targeted immediate relief to alleviate instant distress at birth or on marriage; only claimed by those in need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fund funeral expenses for travelling workers
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocate L20,000 to defray funeral expenses of persons who die while travelling for work and are distant from friends, relieving parishes of this charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improves humane treatment of sick strangers and prevents local parish burden-shifting and harsh treatment of the dead poor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metropolitan asylum for casual poor with work for board and lodging
rubrics_metrics.description: Erect or repurpose buildings to contain at least 6,000 persons offering varied employments; receive all without inquiry; work in exchange for meals and warm lodging; reserve part of earnings to be paid on departure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If each person stayed three months, would assist 24,000 persons yearly. Proposed costing: remaining L20,000 plus L20,000 from coal-tax produce; if labour covers half expenses, L40,000 additional defrays charges. Intended to prevent starvation, petty crime, and provide immediate relief in a metropolis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission policy for metropolitan asylums: no inquiry and flexible stays
rubrics_metrics.description: Receive all applicants without enquiring who or what they are; condition is only that for hours worked each person receives meals and lodging and a portion of their earnings is reserved for them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to eliminate barriers to access, reduce bureaucracy, and give immediate shelter and means to recover; fosters rotation and rehabilitation rather than punitive relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer direct, visible tax reliefs to indirect duty reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid attempting to relieve consumers by abolishing duties charged in gross (per barrel, hogshead, etc.) because abolition may not meaningfully reduce retail prices (example: 3 shillings per barrel on beer reduces purchase only half a farthing per pint).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select relief measures where the benefit is direct, visible, and immediately operative for consumers (e.g., abolish poor-rates or remit tax to poor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use surplus taxes and excise collections as funding source
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw money necessary for the relief program from the excise collections (made eight times a year in every market town) and from surplus current expenses after reducing government costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical administrative instruction for funding: leverage existing periodic excise collection infrastructure and reallocate surplus freed by cuts in current expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce military/naval establishments via alliance; ship-for-ship reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Alliance with France would make many fleets and armies unnecessary; national expenses may be put back to the level when nations were not enemies, with reductions made ship-for-ship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political/diplomatic reform (ending continental intrigue and foreign dominion) is precondition to achieve large military savings; historical precedent (pre-1688/Hanover) used as guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide life annuities/pensions for disbanded soldiers and equivalent officer pay
rubrics_metrics.description: Disband 15,000 soldiers and grant each three shillings per week for life; pay the officers of disbanded corps the same sum as allowed to the men; admit same sum for disbanded navy—total annual cost estimated ~L507,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transition support for those unfitted to other trades; propose combining disbandment with a modest increase in pay for remaining soldiers and navymen; part of recurring half-million cost will lapse over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prudential principle: public money originates from labour and poverty
rubrics_metrics.description: Public money is 'not the produce of riches only, but of the hard earnings of labour and poverty' and should be handled with scrupulous honour and restraint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral grounding for frugality and prioritizing relief: taxation levied from the poor imposes a duty on government to use funds humanely and efficiently; rhetorical justification for all proposed economies and reliefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerated program of relief priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Final enumeration of priorities: (1) Abolition of two millions poor-rates; (2) Provision for 250,000 poor families; (3) Education for 1,030,000 children; (4) Comfortable provision for 140,000 aged persons; (5) Donation of 20s for 50,000 births; (6) 20s for 20,000 marriages; (7) L20,000 for funeral expenses of travelling workers; (8) Employment for casual poor in London/Westminster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as a concise checklist of the plan's deliverables and budgeting targets; intended to replace poor-laws and reduce litigation and misery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative oversight via parish ministers' joint certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Ministers of every parish, of every denomination, to certify jointly to an office that children receiving the allowance are attending school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use local religious and civil notables to enforce attendance conditions, creating a low-cost verification mechanism and shared accountability across denominations.
